q: What is the Phenomenal Deep Glow Facial?
a: Our signature facial — $170 for seventy-five minutes. Deep cleansing combined with cold infusion therapy. It is good for dullness, congestion, puffiness, and the tiredness that shows in the face and does not lift with sleep. The cold calms inflammation and redness, temporarily tightens the look of pores, and helps serums absorb rather than sit on the surface. No downtime.

q: What is your signature treatment?
a: The Phenomenal Deep Glow Facial, $170 for seventy-five minutes. It is the treatment most first visits begin with, and the one we suggest when you are not sure what you need.

q: What is a Hydrafacial and how much is it?
a: The Hydrafacial Treatment is $175 for sixty minutes. It cleanses, exfoliates, extracts and infuses hydrating serum in one pass, using gentle suction rather than manual extraction — so extractions without the pinching. It is good for clogged pores, blackheads, uneven texture and dehydration. There is no downtime at all, and skin looks better leaving than arriving.

q: What is the Golden Dew Hydration Facial?
a: $270 for ninety minutes. It layers moisture-locking ingredients in successive passes. Good for dry, tight, dehydrated skin, skin that drinks product and stays thirsty, fine lines that are really dehydration lines, and post-travel or winter skin. No downtime.

q: What is the Oxygen Facial?
a: $130 for sixty minutes. Pressurised oxygen drives vitamins and serums into the skin for an immediate plumped, luminous look. This is the event facial, ideal two days before a wedding, a shoot or a birthday. It is the gentlest and least expensive facial we offer, which makes it a lovely first treatment. No downtime.

q: What is the Luminous Oxygen Dome Facial?

q: What is dermaplaning and how much is it?
a: Dermaplaning with Ultra Glow Facial is $350 for ninety minutes. A sterile blade removes the fine vellus hair and dead surface layer, followed by a glow-boosting treatment. Skin is immediately smooth, makeup sits flawlessly instead of catching, and everything you apply afterwards absorbs properly. No downtime, though skin is briefly more sun-sensitive.

q: Will dermaplaning make my hair grow back thicker or darker?
a: No. Vellus hair returns exactly as it was. This is the most common question we are asked about dermaplaning, and the answer is a straightforward no.

q: Can I have dermaplaning if I have acne?

q: What is the Nano RevitaGlow Infusion Facial?
a: $290 for sixty minutes. An ultra-fine tip creates microscopic pathways in the very top layer of skin so targeted serums reach deeper than they otherwise could. Good for fine lines, dullness, uneven tone, and skin that no longer responds to topical products. Minimal downtime, with some flushing for a few hours.

q: How is nano infusion different from microneedling?
a: Nano infusion works at the surface rather than puncturing deeper into the skin, so there is no bleeding and no recovery period. It is the gentler option, and a good choice if you want results without a visible recovery week. We do not offer microneedling.

q: What is the Duo Deep Cleansing and Tightening?

q: What is the Traditional Lymphatic Facial?
a: $360 for ninety minutes. A manual technique using slow, rhythmic, precise hand movements to stimulate lymphatic flow and move retained fluid away from the face. q: Why is the Lymphatic Facial your most expensive facial?

q: What is the Gua Sha Sculpting Facial?

q: What is HIFU?
a: HIFU is high-intensity focused ultrasound. Energy is focused at a set depth beneath the skin, heating tissue in tiny precise points to prompt contraction and new collagen formation, without breaking the surface. Our Phenomenal HIFU Lift is $350 for sixty minutes.

q: How much is HIFU?
a: The Phenomenal HIFU Lift is $350 for sixty minutes. The Lift & Sculpt Duo, which combines HIFU with LDM therapy, is $550.

q: What is HIFU good for?
a: Laxity along the jawline, the brow, under the chin and the neck — the softening of definition that tends to begin in the late thirties and forties. It is the answer for someone who wants firmness without surgery and without looking done.

q: How quickly will I see results from HIFU?
a: Results are gradual rather than immediate, building over roughly two to three months as collagen forms. That is exactly why it does not look done. The effect is commonly described as lasting around a year, and it is repeatable.

q: Does HIFU hurt?
a: Some guests feel warmth or brief prickling during treatment. There is no downtime, though there may be mild tenderness for a day or two.

q: Do you offer a non-surgical facelift?
a: Yes. Our Phenomenal HIFU Lift uses focused ultrasound rather than surgery — $350 for an hour, with no recovery time.

q: Will HIFU fill my lines or add volume?
a: HIFU lifts and firms, but it does not add volume or fill lines. It works on laxity rather than on hollowness.

q: What is the Lift & Sculpt Duo?
a: $550 for sixty minutes. It combines the HIFU lift with LDM — Local Dynamic Micromassage — a high-frequency ultrasound working at a much shallower, cellular level to calm inflammation and support skin quality. HIFU works deep for structure while LDM works shallow for quality, which is why they are paired. It is our most complete non-surgical result. No downtime.

q: What is the Plasma Pen treatment?
a: Plasma Pen Skin Tightening is $300 for ninety minutes. A plasma arc creates a controlled pattern of tiny surface points on the skin, and as those heal the tissue contracts and tightens. It is particularly suited to fine, crepey skin in areas nothing else reaches well — the upper eyelid, under the eye, and fine lines around the mouth.

q: Does the Plasma Pen have downtime?
a: Yes, and it is worth planning around. Tiny dark carbon crusts form at each treated point and take roughly five to seven days to flake away on their own. During that week it is visible. They must not be picked at, and the area needs protecting from sun.

q: What can I do about hooded or heavy eyelids?
a: Our Plasma Pen Skin Tightening at $300 is the treatment for crepey skin and hooded lids where nothing topical reaches. One thing to know before booking: tiny dark points form and take about five to seven days to flake away, so it is visible for roughly a week.

q: What is the Japanese Head Spa?
a: $120 for sixty minutes. Scalp therapy in the Japanese tradition, with meticulous cleansing, steam, and extended massage of the scalp, neck and shoulders. Good for product build-up, an itchy or congested scalp, scalp health as the foundation of hair health, and tension held in the head, neck and jaw. Many guests describe it as the most restful hour they have had in months. Hair is washed and dried, with no downtime.

q: What is the Korean Head Spa?
a: $140 for seventy-five minutes. Deep cleansing using herbal-infused scalp solutions in the Korean tradition. It is the more corrective of the two, and suits a congested, flaky, oily or irritated scalp specifically. No downtime.

q: Should I choose the Japanese or the Korean head spa?
a: Japanese leans toward ritual, massage and relaxation. Korean leans toward deep cleansing and scalp correction with herbal solutions, and runs fifteen minutes longer. Choose Japanese to unwind, and Korean if the scalp itself is the problem.

q: What is the Premium Asian Scalp Ritual?
a: $180 for ninety minutes — a fusion of both traditions, combining the Japanese massage ritual with the Korean herbal cleansing. It is the complete experience, the best gift on our menu, and what we would suggest if you are worn down and not quite sure what you need.
